CERT-In flags unauthorised transactions at financial service providers amid cyberattacks

The cyber agency said attackers manipulated business records and payment approvals, while warning of AI-driven attacks across multiple sectors.

Reuters

21 November, 2026 04:20 pm IST

India’s cyber agency said on Friday it had reported unauthorised transactions at service providers for banking and financial services entities, and also at technology service providers supporting government-linked payments.

• Payment fraud incidents extended beyond the financial sector to vendors and partner payout platforms, cyber agency CERT-In said in an advisory on Friday

• Attackers altered business records or approval relationships and then used legitimate payment processes, it said. It did not say how much money had been improperly paid out, or by whom

Show Full Article

• The agency also said that it identified the use of AI-driven frameworks in cyberattacks across different sectors, and issued several recommendations for government organisations, non-financial payout platforms and technology service providers

• India has seen a spate of cyberattacks on banks and non-bank lenders in recent weeks, even as authorities issued warnings and the Reserve Bank of India tightened cybersecurity checks

• Earlier this month, CERT-In named the hacking group behind a wave of AI-driven attacks on financial firms and identified its tools, at least two of them linked to China

• Late last month, India’s central bank warned banks of rising cyberattacks on financial infrastructure, seeking proof of compliance with existing rules and details of their preparedness for AI-related risks

China is expanding the use of 5G across its manufacturing sector, with more than 26,000 private industrial 5G networks built nationwide, China Central Television said on Saturday.

The country’s industrial internet now covers all 41 major industrial categories, while 1,260 5G factories have been built, according to the state broadcaster.

China is also developing 6G technology, with researchers testing its ability to sense the movement of objects, which could eventually support applications including autonomous driving, said CCTV.

Nov 21 (Reuters) – A tanker sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was hit on its stern by an unidentified projectile about 11 nautical miles north of Oman’s Khasab, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Saturday.

No injuries were reported, while the environmental impact of the incident was unknown, UKMTO said.

Khasab lies on Oman’s Musandam Peninsula at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic waterway that carried nearly one-fifth of global crude oil supplies before the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

Show Full Article

Shipping through the strait has been disrupted since Iran moved to close the waterway following the eruption of the conflict on February 28.

(Reporting by Muhammad Al Gebaly and Eman Abouhassira; Editing by Kirsten Donovan)

CAPE TOWN, Nov 21 (Reuters) – South Africa’s first female deputy president, Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who also served as UN under-secretary-general and executive director of UN Women, has died at the age of 71, the presidency said late on Friday.

• Elected as a member of parliament in 1994 in South Africa’s first democratic government, former teacher Mlambo-Ngcuka served as deputy president of South Africa from 2005 to 2008

• Before becoming deputy president, a role in which she oversaw government initiatives to reduce poverty with a focus on women, Mlambo-Ngcuka served as the minister of minerals and energy and as a deputy minister in the Department of Trade and Industry

Show Full Article

• In August 2013 she took the oath of office as executive director of UN Women, serving two terms at an organization created to lead the UN’s work on advancing gender equality and women’s empowerment

(Reporting by Wendell Roelf; Editing by Tom Hogue)
